sections.h2: Where do I find and record property records in King County, Texas?
sections.html:
The King County Clerk in Guthrie records deeds and other real property papers for the county, and the clerk's page links to an online records search. The office sits at 800 South Baker, Guthrie, TX 79236, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 135 at the same ZIP code. The clerk's telephone is 806.596.4412 and the fax line is 806.596.4664.

The clerk's page asks anyone who mails in a document for recording to include a self-addressed envelope. Call before you mail a check, because the page does not print a fee total next to the instructions. Hours are not posted on the page either, so confirm them when you phone.

  • The original signed and acknowledged deed, not a photocopy
  • A mailing address for each grantee, since a missing one can add a charge
  • A self-addressed return envelope
  • A check for the amount the clerk quotes by phone

sections.h2: Which King County offices handle which part of a property file?
sections.html:
Three Guthrie offices cover most of what a seller needs: the clerk for recorded documents, the chief appraiser for value and exemptions, and the tax assessor-collector for bills. Each lists a separate post office box on the county website.

King County office contacts as printed on the county website
OfficeWhat it handlesContact printed on the county site
County ClerkRecorded deeds, liens and other instrumentsP.O. Box 135, Guthrie, TX 79236; 806.596.4412
Chief AppraiserAppraised value, exemption files, King County CAD websiteP.O. Box 117, Guthrie, TX 79236; 806.596.4588
Tax Assessor-CollectorTax statements and paymentsP.O. Box 105, Guthrie, TX 79236; 806.596.4318

The appraisal office also posts its board meeting notices on the county page, which is useful if you want to see when the board that oversees valuations next sits.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the King County Clerk will record it?
sections.html:
A deed has to be signed and acknowledged, or sworn before two witnesses, before a Texas county clerk can record it (Property Code 12.001(b)). The Texas county clerk manual for 2023 lists the instruments that go into the deed records: general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, releases of deeds of trust, leases, powers of attorney and several kinds of affidavit.

The same manual describes how the fee is built. The first page carries a $5.00 charge and each extra page $4.00 under Local Government Code 118.012, and separate records management, archive and technology charges are added on top. Because counties set the add-ons within caps, the clerk's total will not match the base figure, so ask the King County office what the whole bill comes to.

Deeds are filed in the county where the land lies. A house in King County is recorded in Guthrie even if the seller lives in Lubbock, Wichita Falls or out of state.

sections.h2: What kind of county is King County, Texas?
sections.html:
King County is one of the least populated counties in the country, with a Census Bureau estimate of 192 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 265 and the 2010 count was 286, so the trend runs downward. The county covers 910.87 square miles of land, or about 0.3 people per square mile.

The Handbook of Texas places King County in the Rolling Prairie region of northwest Texas, bordered by Cottle, Foard, Knox, Stonewall and Dickens counties. The legislature created it on August 21, 1876, and it was organized in 1891 with Guthrie as the county seat. Large ranches shaped its history, among them the Four Sixes, the Pitchfork, the Matador and the SMS. Oil was found in 1943, and beef cattle still lead agriculture. U.S. Highway 83 runs north to south and U.S. Highway 82 east to west. Dumont and Finney are the other named communities.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 count 177 housing units, 111 households and 1.90 people per household. Owners occupy 59.5 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied unit is $52,100. About 22.9 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: What record problems come up when selling a house in King County?
sections.html:
The usual snags are an owner who died without clearing title, an old lien that was never released, and a tax bill that went unpaid. Each one shows up in the clerk's recorded documents or the tax office files, and each has a state-defined fix.

  • Owner died, no probate. A will can be probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit works only when the estate has no will, assets of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property, and agreement among the heirs. A court must approve it.
  • Heirship by affidavit. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, but no law forces a title company or lender to accept it.
  • Old mortgage. A release of a deed of trust is recorded the same way as any other instrument. Ask the lender for a signed release if the payoff happened years ago.
  • Ranch or oil land. If the parcel is part of larger acreage, ask the title company to trace whether minerals were reserved in earlier deeds.

A title company searches liens, judgments and unresolved heirs before closing, so these items surface before a buyer funds the sale.

sections.h2: How do King County property taxes fit into a sale?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so King County's bills come from local taxing units on values set by the appraisal district as of January 1. The chief appraiser sends notices of value in spring, and a protest generally has to be filed by May 15 or within 30 days after the notice is delivered, whichever is later.

Bills go out around October 1 and are due by January 31. Anything unpaid on February 1 is delinquent, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest added that day. A tax lien attaches to the property every January 1 and secures that year's tax, so a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid. Contact the King County Tax Assessor-Collector for the amount owed on a specific parcel.

For rates and exemptions, see our King County property tax guide.

sections.h2: How can a cash sale work when the King County records are messy?
sections.html:
A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is can close even when the deed history needs cleanup, because the cleanup runs through the title company instead of through repairs and showings. Tell us what you found in the records, such as a missing heir or an old lien, and we will say how a sale would move forward.

Closing papers are recorded with the King County Clerk afterward. Expect the title company to confirm payoff figures for any recorded mortgage and to collect any tax due at closing.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in King County, Texas?
faqs.a: The King County Clerk in Guthrie records deeds. The Texas county clerk acts as the county recorder, and deeds are filed in the county where the property sits, so every King County house is recorded at that one office.

faqs.q: Can I send a deed to the King County Clerk by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, the clerk's page asks mailers to include a self-addressed envelope. Call 806.596.4412 first for the fee, and send the original signed and acknowledged deed with a grantee mailing address.

faqs.q: Where do I dispute my King County appraisal?
faqs.a: Start with the chief appraiser at P.O. Box 117 in Guthrie. A written protest goes to the appraisal review board by May 15 or 30 days after the notice of value is delivered, whichever is later.

faqs.q: What if the owner of a King County house died without probate?
faqs.a: Options include probate of a will within four years, a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding homestead, a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship. Which one fits depends on whether there was a will and who the heirs are.

faqs.q: How many people live in King County, Texas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 192 residents as of July 1, 2025, down from 265 counted in the 2020 census. It reports 177 housing units and a median owner-occupied home value of $52,100 for 2020 to 2024.
